diagnostic_evidence.quote: (1) the uniform rate matrix: $\lambda(\vy, \vx) = d^{-1}$ only if $\|\vy-\vx\|_0 = 1$
In practice, a usual setting of the state space is $\sX = [S]^d$, where $S$ is the number of states in each dimension.

issues.failure_explanation: On $\sX=[S]^d$ the displayed conditional must sum to 1 over $\vx_t$, but each coordinate factor sums to $e^{-t}+S(1-e^{-t})/d$, equal to 1 only when $S=d$; e.g. for $d=1$ it gives $p_{t|0}(x_t=x_0)=1$ and $p_{t|0}(x_t\ne x_0)=0$. It is also inconsistent with the stated rate $\lambda=d^{-1}$ to each of the $(S-1)d$ one-coordinate-different states, for which the per-coordinate law is $e^{-(S-1)t/d}\delta_{x_0^i}+(1-e^{-(S-1)t/d})/(S-1)$; no choice of $S,d$ makes the displayed formula correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the rate/formula pair by a consistent one (e.g. per-coordinate rate $(S-1)^{-1}$ with $\prod_i(e^{-t}\delta_{x_0^i}+(1-e^{-t})/(S-1))$, or state the conditional actually induced by the rate $d^{-1}$).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed closed-form transition for the uniform rate matrix in the discrete-diffusion background (Sec. 2.3), used to illustrate the discrete score-matching loss, is unreliable; no main framework result relies on it.
issues.title: Uniform rate matrix conditional formula is not a probability distribution
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a background formula; all framework theorems, guarantees, and the advertised scope are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \gL^{h, \lambda} f = h^{-1} \gL(h f) - h^{-1} f \gL h = \gL f + h^{-1} \Gamma(h, f),
In particular, choosing $\lambda = h^{-1} \gL h$ results in a consedrvative transformed process, \emph{i.e.}, $\gL^{h, \lambda} 1 = 1$, satisfying

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated definition the identity $\gL^{h,\lambda}f=\gL f+h^{-1}\Gamma(h,f)$ is false: for $\gL=\frac12\Delta$ in 1D with $h=e^x$, $f=x$, the left side equals 1 while $h^{-1}(h\gL(h^{-1}f)-f\gL h^{-1})=\frac{x-2}{2}e^{-x}-\frac{x}{2}e^{-2x}$. The identity holds only with the standard carre du champ $\Gamma(h,f)=\gL(hf)-h\gL f-f\gL h$, which is the definition used everywhere else in the paper (thm:time_reversal, lem:alpha). Separately, a conservative generator satisfies $\gL^{h,\lambda}1=0$, not $1$.

failure_location.quote: where $\Gamma(h, f) = h \gL(h^{-1} f) - f \gL h^{-1}$ is the carr\'e du champ operator associated with the generator $\gL$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $\Gamma(h,f)=\gL(hf)-h\gL f-f\gL h$ in thm:doob and correct $\gL^{h,\lambda}1=1$ to $\gL^{h,\lambda}1=0$.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed formulas of thm:doob, the motivational result for the conservative Doob transform behind ass:K and lem:alpha, are false as written; no downstream result invokes the erroneous operator definition.
issues.title: Carre du champ is misdefined in the generalized Doob h-transform theorem
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction to a cited background theorem; the framework uses the correct carre du champ elsewhere, so no inference or guarantee needs repair.

issues.failure_explanation: The appendix derivation obtains the adjoint eq:adjoint_levy by integrating the generator's small-jump compensation by parts, then plugs it into thm:time_reversal_app. For any infinite-activity Levy measure the displayed compensation term contains $-d\,g(\vx)\int_{B(\vx,1)}\lambda_t(\dif\vy,\vx)=-\infty$, and the jump term $\int(\lambda_t(\vx,\vy)g(\vy)-\lambda_t(\vy,\vx)g(\vx))\dif\vy$ diverges whenever $\int_{B(\vx,1)}\|\vy-\vx\|\lambda_t(\dif\vy,\vx)=\infty$, so eq:adjoint_levy is ill-defined and the manipulations invalid; ass:regularity_levy still permits such measures (a $C^{1,0}$ density vanishing on the diagonal need not have finite activity). Moreover the paper's own instances violate ass:regularity_levy: the alpha-stable kernel of ex:alpha_stable is singular at $\vy=\vx$ (not $C^{1,0}$, not $0$ on the diagonal), and the pure-jump model sets $\mD_t\equiv0$, contradicting the required positive definiteness. Only the principal-value interpretation of $\gI$ is acknowledged.

issues.failure_explanation: With drift $-\vx/\alpha$ and the alpha-stable measure of eq:alpha_stable, the conditional law of $\vx_t$ is stable with exponent $(1-e^{-t})\|\xi\|^\alpha$ shifted by $e^{-t/\alpha}\vx_0$; direct evaluation of the paper's own Fourier formula gives $\gI[p_{t|0}(\cdot|\vx_0)](\vx_t)=-(\vx_t-e^{-t/\alpha}\vx_0)/(1-e^{-t})$, without the factor $1/\alpha$. issues.overall_effect: The regression target of the LIM loss in ex:alpha_stable and the claimed closed form 'enabling efficient training and inference' are wrong by a factor of $\alpha$; the structure of the example is otherwise unaffected.
issues.title: Closed-form integral term in the alpha-stable example is off by a factor of alpha

issues.failure_explanation: The score identity only factors out $1/\hat s(\vy^{\mathrm{ref}},\vy_t^{(k)})$; the remaining integral $\int\hat s(\vy^{\mathrm{ref}},\vy)\lambda(\|\vy-\vy_t^{(k)}\|)\dif\vy$ still depends on $\vy_t^{(k)}$ through the center of the isotropic kernel, so it does not equal $\gJ[\cev\lambda^\varphi_t(\cdot,\vy^{\mathrm{ref}})]$, whose kernel is centered at $\vy^{\mathrm{ref}}$. issues.title: Jump-model backward simulation integral-reuse identity is false
issues.why_classification: A false local implementation shortcut with a straightforward bypass already used elsewhere in the paper; no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed exponential is of bounded variation and is not the density martingale: the correct Girsanov/Doob density is the ratio form derived first in the proof, and it differs from the stated exponential by $\exp(M_t)$, where $M_t=\log\eta_{T-t}(\cev x_t)-\log\eta_T(\cev x_0)-\int_0^t\tilde{\cev\gL}\log\eta_{T-s}(\cev x_s)\dif s$ is a nonzero martingale (e.g. for a two-state chain with $\eta=(1,e)$ one checks $\E[W_T]\neq1$, so the stated expression is not even a probability density).
